desk_desc: Armed and waiting for a setup worth flying.

receipts.headline: We opened the same playbook on new ground
receipts.lesson: Proving one person and a fleet of agents can build something real shouldn't stop at one place — so we began applying the same disciplined, receipt-first playbook to new ground, in parallel, without disturbing what already runs.

receipts.headline: Our first test on new ground came back "no"
receipts.lesson: We put one of our new ideas through a pass/fail rule fixed in advance; the honest answer was "no", so we kept the receipt and moved on — a "no" is a finding, not a setback.

receipts.headline: We made our own website heal itself
receipts.lesson: A site that claims a company runs itself must not go stale — so it now rebuilds from the record every hour and speaks up only when it genuinely can't fix itself.

receipts.headline: We decided how we'd be proven wrong, first
receipts.lesson: Before running a test of one of our own ideas, we committed the pass/fail rule to the record — so when the answer came back "no", we couldn't argue with it.

receipts.headline: We broke our own system on purpose
receipts.lesson: We injected faults into the live system to see if it would tell on itself; the health report came back FAILED, which was exactly the result we wanted.
